image_prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create a new 16:9 single photograph as the exact opening frame for an instructional live-action continuity example. Reference 1 is the sole identity authority for fictional adult Claire: keep her actual naturally asymmetrical eyes, eye spacing, nose bridge, muted mouth shape, jaw and apparent age, straight black bangs and low ponytail, small gold hoops, slate blue cotton shirt. Reference 2 is exclusively the scene and framing guide: keep the walnut workshop table, window light from screen-left, dark walnut lower wall against matte beige above, seated medium view, natural skin and cotton. Replace the mug with one realistic compact folded red nylon travel umbrella, no mug anywhere. Horizontal folded umbrella, black short handle at screen-left and small capped tip at screen-right, a visibly wrapped fastening strap and folded nylon panels, modest 26 cm scale against the width of her shoulders. The umbrella's full length is visible with a clean, roughly palm-height space under its length from the real tabletop. Claire's anatomical right hand, which appears on frame-left, naturally supports the umbrella near its balance point with fingers around the fabric barrel near the strap. Her other hand rests palm-down on the table well away from the umbrella. Show both wrists and hands with plausible knuckles, avoid split fingers and accidental grips. The body is relaxed, neck upright with a slight chin dip and eyes visibly looking at the umbrella, not in lens. Front three-quarter upper-body medium framing with the head, eyes, both hands, full umbrella and illuminated tabletop readable. Use natural local contrast around the dark handle, tip and table gap while keeping soft daylight. Restrained everyday camera color and real materials, one frame only. No writing, brands, overlays or extra objects.

video_plan.common_prompt: Exactly two photoreal shots with one hard cut at about 3.0s. Start from the supplied medium frame. Claire looks at the folded umbrella while seated at the walnut worktable. A soft window on frame-left lights the blue-gray cotton, matte nylon and walnut grain. Shot 1 is fixed; shot 2 is a fixed tighter view from the same side of the action axis. Both show the umbrella tip and the tabletop with a clear margin. The left hand rests at the far side of the table. The right hand holds the strap side of a single folded red umbrella. Keep the physical grip, clothing, light and space plausible. Natural breathing, no extra gestures. The umbrella is placed on the tabletop once and the right hand releases from the resting umbrella. Native quiet workshop air, a light nylon brush during the move, one soft wood tap on actual contact. No dialogue, music or sounds on the cut itself.

directions.label: E20-A
directions.prompt: In the wider shot Claire starts to lower the folded umbrella. At the cut, go closer and continue the lowering action until the umbrella rests on the table. Hold briefly.

directions.label: E20-B
directions.prompt: In the wider shot Claire holds the folded umbrella at its starting height above the tabletop, parallel to the front edge, black handle toward camera-left, tip right, with the same right-hand grip. Keep that still in the last frame before the cut and the first frame after the cut. Keep the tip and handle on the same sides. After the cut, lower in one continuous move, make contact once and release once around 4.8s. Hold briefly.
